questions.question: A sum becomes 2 times in 4 years at simple interest. In how many years the same sum will become 16 times?
questions.questionHtml: A sum becomes 2 times in 4 years at simple interest. In how many years the same sum will become 16 times?
questions.solution:
If a sum becomes n1 times in t1 years and n2 times in t2 years at SI:

(n1 − 1) / t1 = (n2 − 1) / t2

(2 − 1) / 4 = (16 − 1) / t2

1 / 4 = 15 / t2

t2 = 15 × 4 = 60 years.

questions.question: Rs 30000 became Rs 42000 in 8 years. If the investment was made on simple interest, what was the rate on simple interest offered per annum?
questions.questionHtml: Rs 30000 became Rs 42000 in 8 years. If the investment was made on simple interest, what was the rate on simple interest offered per annum?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total interest percentage over 8 years = (Interest ÷ Principal) × 100

Total Interest % = (12,000 ÷ 30,000) × 100 = 40%

Annual Rate of Interest = Total % ÷ Time

Annual Rate = 40% ÷ 8 = 5%

∴ The correct answer is 5%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Principal (P) = ₹30,000

Amount (A) = ₹42,000

Time (T) = 8 years

Formula Used:

Simple Interest (SI) = Amount − Principal

Rate (R) = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × T)

Calculations:

⇒ SI = 42,000 − 30,000

⇒ SI = ₹12,000

⇒ R = (12,000 × 100) ÷ (30,000 × 8)

⇒ R = 1,200,000 ÷ 240,000

⇒ R = 120 ÷ 24

⇒ R = 5%

∴ The correct answer is 5%.

Additional Information

Simple Interest Property

In Simple Interest, the interest remains constant for every year as it is always calculated on the original Principal.

Sum and Amount Relation

The total Amount after T years is given by A = P × (1 + RT/100).

SI vs CI Difference

For the first year (if compounded annually), Simple Interest and Compound Interest are always equal.

questions.question: What is the simple interest on Rs. 32,000 at 8.5% per annum for period from 10 th Feb., 2019 to 24 th April, 2019?
questions.questionHtml: What is the simple interest on Rs. 32,000 at 8.5% per annum for period from 10<sup style="">th</sup> Feb., 2019 to 24<sup style="">th</sup> April, 2019?
questions.solution:
Total time from 10th Feb to 24th April = 18 + 31 + 24 = 73 days = 1/5 year.

Effective interest rate for 1/5 year = 8.5% ÷ 5 = 1.7%.

Simple Interest = 1.7% of 32000 = (1.7 × 32000) ÷ 100 = Rs. 544.

questions.question: The simple interest on a certain sum for 10 \(\frac{1}{2}\) years at 12% p.a. is Rs. 56 less than the amount of the same sum at 9% p.a. for 3 years at simple interest. The sum (in Rs.) is:
questions.questionHtml: The simple interest on a certain sum for 10\(\frac{1}{2}\) years at 12% p.a. is Rs. 56 less than the amount of the same sum at 9% p.a. for 3 years at simple interest. The sum (in Rs.) is:
questions.solution:
SI at 12% is Rs. 56 less than Amount at 9%

P × 21/2 × 12/100 = P(1 + 27/100) - 56

P × 126/100 = P × 127/100 - 56

127P/100 - 126P/100 = 56

P/100 = 56

P = 5600

questions.question: Aman had Rs.10,000 with him. He lent a part of it at 8% per annum simple interest and the remaining at 10% per annum. His total annual income was Rs. 880 Find the sum lent at 8%
questions.questionHtml: Aman had Rs.10,000 with him. He lent a part of it at 8% per annum simple interest and the remaining at 10% per annum. His total annual income was Rs. 880 Find the sum lent at 8%
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Overall interest rate = (Total Interest ÷ Total Principal) × 100 = (880 ÷ 10,000) × 100 = 8.8%.

Using Alligation: Ratio of sums at 8% and 10% = (10 − 8.8) : (8.8 − 8) = 1.2 : 0.8 = 3 : 2.

Total parts = 3 + 2 = 5 parts → ₹10,000.

Sum lent at 8% = (3 ÷ 5) × 10,000 = ₹6000.

∴ The correct answer is ₹6000.

Alternate Method

Given: Total Principal = ₹10,000, Total Time = 1 year, Total Interest = ₹880.

Formula Used: Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ Let the sum lent at 8% be x and at 10% be (10,000 − x).

⇒ [(x × 8 × 1) ÷ 100] + [((10,000 − x) × 10 × 1) ÷ 100] = 880

⇒ (8x ÷ 100) + (100,000 − 10x) ÷ 100 = 880

⇒ 8x + 100,000 − 10x = 88,000

⇒ −2x = 88,000 − 100,000

⇒ −2x = −12,000

⇒ x = 6000

∴ The correct answer is ₹6000.

Additional Information

Simple Interest Formula

Interest is calculated only on the principal amount: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Weighted Average Rate

When a sum is split, the net rate Rtotal = (P1R1 + P2R2) ÷ (P1 + P2).

Alligation Rule

Used to find the ratio in which two quantities are mixed to get a mean value: (Quantity 1 / Quantity 2) = (Rate 2 − Mean) / (Mean − Rate 1).

questions.question: The total simple interest on Rs 500 in 8 years and Rs 300 in 16 years is Rs 1100. If the rate of interest is equal in both cases. Then find the rate of interest.
questions.questionHtml: The total simple interest on Rs 500 in 8 years and Rs 300 in 16 years is Rs 1100. If the rate of interest is equal in both cases. Then find the rate of interest.
questions.solution:
Let, the rate of interest be R

1100 = (500 × R × 8) / 100 + (300 × R ×16) / 100

⇒ 1100 = (4000 × R) / 100 + (4800 × R) / 100

⇒ 1100 = (40 × R + 48 × R) ⇒ 88R = 1100 ⇒ R = 1100 / 88

⇒ R = 100 / 8 ⇒ R = 12.5 %

questions.question: A sum amounts to Rs. 14,395.20 at 9.25% p.a. simple interest in 5.4 years. What will be the simple interest on the same sum at 8.6% p.a. in 4.5 years?
questions.questionHtml: A sum amounts to Rs. 14,395.20 at 9.25% p.a. simple interest in 5.4 years. What will be the simple interest on the same sum at 8.6% p.a. in 4.5 years?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total interest % for first case = 9.25% × 5.4 = 49.95%

Amount % = 100% + 49.95% = 149.95%

Total interest % for second case = 8.6% × 4.5 = 38.7%

Required SI = (14395.20 ÷ 149.95) × 38.7

Required SI = 96 × 38.7 = 3715.20

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 3,715.20.

Alternate Method

Given: Amount (A1) = Rs. 14,395.20, Rate (R1) = 9.25%, Time (T1) = 5.4 years

Target: SI for Rate (R2) = 8.6%, Time (T2) = 4.5 years

Formula: Amount = P + (P × R × T) ÷ 100 | SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ Amount (A1) = P × (1 + (R1 × T1) ÷ 100)

⇒ 14395.20 = P × (1 + (9.25 × 5.4) ÷ 100)

⇒ 14395.20 = P × (1 + 49.95 ÷ 100) = P × 1.4995

⇒ P = 14395.20 ÷ 1.4995 = Rs. 9600

⇒ SI2 = (P × R2 × T2) ÷ 100

⇒ SI2 = (9600 × 8.6 × 4.5) ÷ 100

⇒ SI2 = 96 × 38.7

⇒ SI2 = Rs. 3715.20

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 3,715.20.

Additional Information

Simple Interest Formula

The basic formula for Simple Interest is SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100, where P is Principal, R is Rate per annum, and T is Time in years.

Effective Rate of Interest

Total interest percentage over T years is (R × T)%. This can be directly added to 100% to find the Amount percentage.

Amount Calculation

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Interest (SI). In terms of percentage, A = P(100 + RT) ÷ 100.

questions.question: A sum of money was put at simple interest at a certain rate for 2 years. If it had been at 1% higher rate, then it would have fetched Rs. 180 more. What is the sum ?
questions.questionHtml: A sum of money was put at simple interest at a certain rate for 2 years. If it had been at 1% higher rate, then it would have fetched Rs. 180 more. What is the sum ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The extra interest is generated by the increased rate over the given time.

Effective increase in interest % = 1% × 2 years = 2%

⇒ 2% of Principal = ₹180

⇒ 100% (Principal) = (180 ÷ 2) × 100 = ₹9000

∴ The correct answer is ₹9000.

Alternate Method

Given: Time (T) = 2 years, Rate Increase = 1% per annum, Extra Interest = ₹180.

Formula Used: Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Let the original Principal be P and original Rate be R.

⇒ Original SI = (P × R × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ New SI = (P × (R + 1) × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ New SI − Original SI = 180

⇒ [(2P × (R + 1)) ÷ 100] − [2PR ÷ 100] = 180

⇒ (2P ÷ 100) × (R + 1 − R) = 180

⇒ 2P ÷ 100 = 180

⇒ P = (180 × 100) ÷ 2

⇒ P = 90 × 100 = 9000

∴ The correct answer is ₹9000.

Additional Information

Simple Interest Property

Simple interest is directly proportional to the principal, rate, and time. If the rate increases by x% for T years, the total interest increases by (P × x × T) ÷ 100.

Rate vs Interest Change

When the principal and time are constant, the ratio of the change in interest is equal to the ratio of the change in rate: (SI1 − SI2) = P × T × (R1 − R2) ÷ 100.

Principal Formula

If the difference in interest (D) is known for a change in rate (r) over time (T), then Principal (P) = (D × 100) ÷ (r × T).

questions.question: In 5 years, the simple interest on an amount of Rs. X is \(\rm \frac{2}{5}^{th}\) of the principal. The rate of interest per annum is:
questions.questionHtml: In 5 years, the simple interest on an amount of Rs. X is \(\rm \frac{2}{5}^{th}\) of the principal. The rate of interest per annum is:
questions.solution:
Simple Interest = (P × R × T) / 100. Given, SI = (2/5)P.

Substituting these values: (2/5)P = (P × R × 5) / 100 ⇒ 2P = 5PR ⇒ R = 40/5 = 8%

questions.question: The simple interest on a certain sum is one-fourth of the sum. If the number of years and the rate of annual interest are numerically equal, then the number of years is
questions.questionHtml: The simple interest on a certain sum is one-fourth of the sum. If the number of years and the rate of annual interest are numerically equal, then the number of years is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When the simple interest is a fraction of the principal and Rate = Time:

Time = √((SI ÷ P) × 100)

Given SI ÷ P = 1 ÷ 4

⇒ Time = √((1 ÷ 4) × 100) = √25 = 5 years

∴ The correct answer is 5 years.

Alternate Method

Given:

Simple Interest (SI) = P ÷ 4

Rate of Interest (R) = Time in years (T)

Formula Used:

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Calculations:

⇒ P ÷ 4 = (P × T × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 1 ÷ 4 = T2 ÷ 100

⇒ T2 = 100 ÷ 4

⇒ T2 = 25

⇒ T = √25 = 5

∴ The correct answer is 5 years.

Additional Information

Direct Formula for Equal Rate and Time

When Simple Interest is 1/n of the principal and the rate percentage equals the time in years, directly apply T = √(100 ÷ n).

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

For the first year, both SI and CI are equal for a given principal and rate of interest. After the first year, CI calculates interest on the accumulated sum.

Rule of 72

A mental math shortcut to estimate the doubling time of an investment under compound interest: Time ≈ 72 ÷ Annual Interest Rate.

questions.question: Shivam invests a sum of ₹5400 and Rupesh invests a sum of ₹9400 at the same rate of simple interest per annum. If, at the end of 4 years, Rupesh gets ₹600 more interest than Shivam, then find the rate of interest per annum (in percentage).
questions.questionHtml: Shivam invests a sum of ₹5400 and Rupesh invests a sum of ₹9400 at the same rate of simple interest per annum. If, at the end of 4 years, Rupesh gets ₹600 more interest than Shivam, then find the rate of interest per annum (in percentage).
questions.solution:
Let the rate of interest per annum be R%.

For Shivam: SI1 = (5400 × R × 4) ÷ 100 = 216R

For Rupesh: SI2 = (9400 × R × 4) ÷ 100 = 376R

Given: SI2 − SI1 = 600 ⇒ 376R − 216R = 600 ⇒ 160R = 600

R = 600 ÷ 160 = 3.75

∴ The rate of interest per annum is 3.75%.

questions.question: A certain sum is lent at 4% p.a. for 3 years, 8% p.a. for the next 4 years, and 12% p.a. beyond 7 years. If for a period of 11 years, the simple interest obtained is Rs. 27,600, then the sum is (in Rs):
questions.questionHtml: A certain sum is lent at 4% p.a. for 3 years, 8% p.a. for the next 4 years, and 12% p.a. beyond 7 years. If for a period of 11 years, the simple interest obtained is Rs. 27,600, then the sum is (in Rs):
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Calculate the total effective interest percentage for the entire period.

Total interest % = (4% × 3 years) + (8% × 4 years) + (12% × 4 years)

Total interest % = 12% + 32% + 48% = 92%

Given, 92% of Sum = ₹27,600

⇒ 1% of Sum = 27,600 ÷ 92 = 300

⇒ 100% (Sum) = 300 × 100 = 30,000

∴ The correct answer is ₹30,000.

Alternate Method

Given:

Rate 1 (R1) = 4%, Time 1 (T1) = 3 years

Rate 2 (R2) = 8%, Time 2 (T2) = 4 years

Rate 3 (R3) = 12%, Time 3 (T3) = 11 − (3 + 4) = 4 years

Total Simple Interest (SI) = ₹27,600

Formula Used:

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Let the Sum be P.

⇒ Total SI = (P × R1 × T1)/100 + (P × R2 × T2)/100 + (P × R3 × T3)/100

⇒ 27600 = (P × 4 × 3)/100 + (P × 8 × 4)/100 + (P × 12 × 4)/100

⇒ 27600 = (12P + 32P + 48P) ÷ 100

⇒ 27600 = 92P ÷ 100

⇒ P = (27600 × 100) ÷ 92

⇒ P = 300 × 100

⇒ P = 30,000

∴ The correct answer is ₹30,000.

Additional Information

Total Amount in Simple Interest

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI). In percentage terms, A = 100% + (R × T)%.

Effective Interest Rate

When rates vary over different time periods, the net effective rate is the sum of (Ratei × Timei) for each period.

Simple Interest Property

Simple interest is always calculated on the original principal throughout the entire duration of the loan.

questions.question: In how much time will an amount be doubled at the rate of 12.5% ?
questions.questionHtml: In how much time will an amount be doubled at the rate of 12.5% ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For a sum of money to double itself at Simple Interest, the generated interest must be exactly equal to the Principal.

In such cases, Time (T) = 100 ÷ Rate (R)

⇒ T = 100 ÷ 12.5

⇒ T = 8 years

∴ The correct answer is 8 years.

Alternate Method

Given:

Rate of Interest (R) = 12.5%

Amount (A) = 2 × Principal (P) = 2P

Formula Used:

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + SI

Calculation:

⇒ SI = A − P

⇒ SI = 2P − P = P

⇒ P = (P × 12.5 × T) ÷ 100

Dividing both sides by P:

⇒ 1 = (12.5 × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 100 = 12.5 × T

⇒ T = 100 ÷ 12.5

⇒ T = 8

∴ The correct answer is 8 years.

Additional Information

Rule for 'n' Times at Simple Interest

If an amount becomes 'n' times of itself at Simple Interest, then Time (T) = 100 × (n − 1) ÷ R, or Rate (R) = 100 × (n − 1) ÷ T.

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

Simple Interest is calculated uniformly on the original principal throughout the loan period. Compound Interest is calculated on the principal along with any accumulated interest from the prior periods.

Rule of 72 (Compound Interest Shortcut)

To determine the approximate time required to double an investment under Compound Interest, simply divide 72 by the annual rate of interest (T ≈ 72 ÷ R).

questions.questionHtml: If a loan grew 3 times in 6 years at Simple Interest, then how much time will it take to grow 8 times?
questions.solution:
T1 / (n1 - 1) = T2 / (n2 - 1)
6 / (3 - 1) = T2 / (8 - 1)
3 = T2 / 7 ⇒ T2 = 21 years

questions.question: Rs.12000 becomes Rs.15000 in 18 months at a certain rate of interest at simple interest. Find the amount if Rs.5000 invested at the same rate for 30 months at simple interest.(approximately)
questions.questionHtml: Rs.12000 becomes Rs.15000 in 18 months at a certain rate of interest at simple interest. Find the amount if Rs.5000 invested at the same rate for 30 months at simple interest.(approximately)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For a constant rate, SI ∝ P × T ⇒ SI1 / SI2 = (P1 × T1) / (P2 × T2)

⇒ 3000 / SI2 = (12000 × 18) / (5000 × 30) = 216 / 150

⇒ SI2 = (3000 × 150) / 216 = 2083.33

⇒ Total Amount = 5000 + 2083.33 ≈ ₹7083

∴ The correct answer is ₹7083.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial Principal (P1) = ₹12000, Initial Amount (A1) = ₹15000

Initial Time (T1) = 18 months = 1.5 years

New Principal (P2) = ₹5000, New Time (T2) = 30 months = 2.5 years

Formula Used:

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) / 100

Calculations:

⇒ SI1 = A1 − P1 = 15000 − 12000 = ₹3000

⇒ 3000 = (12000 × R × 1.5) / 100

⇒ 3000 = 180 × R

⇒ R = 3000 / 180 = 50/3 % p.a.

Now, calculating interest for the second case:

⇒ SI2 = (5000 × (50/3) × 2.5) / 100

⇒ SI2 = 50 × (50/3) × 2.5

⇒ SI2 = 6250 / 3 = ₹2083.33

⇒ Amount (A2) = P2 + SI2

⇒ A2 = 5000 + 2083.33 = ₹7083.33 ≈ ₹7083

∴ The correct answer is ₹7083.

Additional Information

Simple Interest Formula

SI = (P × R × T) / 100, where P is Principal, R is Rate of interest per annum, and T is Time in years.

Amount in Simple Interest

Total Amount = Principal + Simple Interest ⇒ A = P [1 + (R × T) / 100].

Rule of Proportionality

If the rate of interest is constant, Simple Interest is directly proportional to the product of Principal and Time (SI ∝ P × T).

questions.question: A certain sum of money amounts to Rs. 5320 in 3 years at simple interest and to Rs. 5980 in 4 years and 6 months at simple interest. Find the rate of interest.
questions.questionHtml: A certain sum of money amounts to Rs. 5320 in 3 years at simple interest and to Rs. 5980 in 4 years and 6 months at simple interest. Find the rate of interest.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Interest for 1.5 years (4.5 − 3) = 5980 − 5320 = ₹660

Interest for 1 year = 660 ÷ 1.5 = ₹440

Principal = Amount in 3 years − Interest for 3 years = 5320 − (440 × 3) = ₹4000

Rate % = (Interest for 1 year ÷ Principal) × 100 = (440 ÷ 4000) × 100 = 11%

∴ The correct answer is 11%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Amount in 3 years (A1) = ₹5320

Amount in 4.5 years (A2) = ₹5980

Formula: Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100 | Amount = P + SI

⇒ SI for (4.5 − 3) years = 5980 − 5320

⇒ SI for 1.5 years = ₹660

⇒ SI for 1 year = 660 ÷ 1.5 = ₹440

⇒ SI for 3 years = 440 × 3 = ₹1320

⇒ Principal (P) = A1 − SI for 3 years = 5320 − 1320 = ₹4000

⇒ Rate (R) = (SI1yr × 100) ÷ P

⇒ Rate (R) = (440 × 100) ÷ 4000

⇒ Rate (R) = 11%

∴ The correct answer is 11%.

Additional Information

Simple Interest Formula

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100, where P is Principal, R is Rate per annum, and T is Time in years.

Amount Calculation

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI). In SI, the interest remains constant for every equal time interval.

Finding Principal from Two Amounts

If a sum becomes A1 in T1 years and A2 in T2 years, SI for 1 year = (A2 − A1) ÷ (T2 − T1).

SI vs CI

Simple interest is calculated only on the principal, while Compound Interest is calculated on the principal plus accumulated interest.

questions.question: A certain sum of money becomes 5 times in 15 years when invested at simple interest. In how much time (years and months) will is becomes 12 times itself at the same rate at simple interest?
questions.questionHtml: A certain sum of money becomes 5 times in 15 years when invested at simple interest. In how much time (years and months) will is becomes 12 times itself at the same rate at simple interest?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For Simple Interest, use the ratio: (n1 − 1) / T1 = (n2 − 1) / T2

Here, n1 = 5, T1 = 15 years and n2 = 12, T2 = ?

⇒ (5 − 1) / 15 = (12 − 1) / T2

⇒ 4 / 15 = 11 / T2

⇒ T2 = (15 × 11) / 4 = 165 / 4 = 41.25 years

∴ The correct answer is 41 years 3 months.

Alternate Method

Given:

Case 1: Principal (P) becomes 5P in 15 years.

Case 2: Principal (P) becomes 12P in 'T' years.

Formula used:

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) / 100

Amount (A) = P + SI

Calculations:

In Case 1:

⇒ SI1 = 5P − P = 4P

⇒ 4P = (P × R × 15) / 100

⇒ R = (4 × 100) / 15 = 80/3 %

In Case 2:

⇒ SI2 = 12P − P = 11P

⇒ 11P = (P × (80/3) × T) / 100

⇒ 11 = (80 × T) / 300

⇒ T = (11 × 300) / 80

⇒ T = 330 / 8 = 165 / 4 = 41.25 years

Converting decimal years to months:

⇒ 0.25 years = 0.25 × 12 months = 3 months

⇒ T = 41 years 3 months

∴ The correct answer is 41 years 3 months.

Additional Information

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

In Simple Interest, the interest is calculated only on the initial Principal, while in Compound Interest, interest is calculated on the Principal plus any accumulated interest.

Rate of Interest in SI

Rate (R) = (SI × 100) / (P × T). This shows that for a constant Principal, the interest earned is directly proportional to Time and Rate.

SI for Multiples of Sum

If a sum becomes 'n' times itself, the Simple Interest earned is (n − 1) times the Principal.
